changes.before: However, global economic and financial developments continue to pose risks.
The Committee continues to monitor inflation developments closely.
changes.after: The Committee continues to closely monitor inflation indicators and global economic and financial developments.

changes.before: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in January suggests that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate pace despite the global economic and financial developments of recent months.
changes.after: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in March indicates that labor market conditions have improved further even as growth in economic activity appears to have slowed.

changes.before: Household spending has been increasing at a moderate rate, and the housing sector has improved further; however, business fixed investment and net exports have been soft.
changes.after: Growth in household spending has moderated, although households' real income has risen at a solid rate and consumer sentiment remains high.

changes.before: Inflation picked up in recent months; however, it continued to run below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective, partly reflecting declines in energy prices and in prices of non-energy imports.
changes.after: Inflation has continued to run below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective, partly reflecting earlier declines in energy prices and falling prices of non-energy imports.

parsed.rationale: Dropping the explicit statement that global developments 'continue to pose risks' removes a key dovish hedge and keeps a near-term hike in play, a modestly hawkish signal. This is only partly offset by a softer read on growth and spending and the removal of 'inflation picked up', while the policy guidance is otherwise unchanged.

spans.quote: However, global economic and financial developments continue to pose risks.
The Committee continues to monitor inflation developments closely.

Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in January suggests that economic activity has been expanding at a moderate pace despite the global economic and financial developments of recent months.
Household spending has been increasing at a moderate rate, and the housing sector has improved further; however, business fixed investment and net exports have been soft.

Inflation picked up in recent months; however, it continued to run below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective, partly reflecting declines in energy prices and in prices of non-energy imports.
The Committee continues to closely monitor inflation indicators and global economic and financial developments.
Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in March indicates that labor market conditions have improved further even as growth in economic activity appears to have slowed.
Growth in household spending has moderated, although households' real income has risen at a solid rate and consumer sentiment remains high.
Inflation has continued to run below the Committee's 2 percent longer-run objective, partly reflecting earlier declines in energy prices and falling prices of non-energy imports.
